notes: Background: mid-market product analytics SaaS (B2B). Customer-facing chat assistant + similarity search for docs and help center.
Trial results (hosted API): ~23k generation requests, ~12k embedding calls over 2 weeks. Observed token mix: ~60% short chat (<=512 tokens), ~25% long chat (512-2048 tokens), ~15% embeddings.
Measured latencies on hosted: p50 ~120-160ms, p95 ~320-420ms for text-gen; embeddings p95 ~180ms. They want Dedicated p50 <=100ms, p95 <=250ms.

Traffic profile: current steady QPS ~6-12, observed daily peak bursts to 18-22 QPS sustained for minutes; stress test showed short bursts up to 45 QPS (10s). Concurrency during peak ~28-40 concurrent streams.
Token assumptions for sizing: avg generation tokens per request (prompt+resp) ~1,350; avg embedding token accounting per call ~512. Current tokens/day ~1.8M tokens (generation + embedding combined).
Forecast request growth: 3x over 6 months with product launch to new enterprise customers; expected steady-state QPS target 35-60, peak bursts 80-120 QPS in 6-9 months.
POC / Dedicated sizing ask from customer: baseline capacity to cover current peak (45 QPS) with room to autoscale to forecast peak (120 QPS). Prefer predictable reserved baseline + burst buffer.

Prelim Redwood sizing recommendation: reserved pool = 3 x A100-80GB equiv (handles baseline 40-50 QPS with Kv-cache + batching), autoscale up to 8 nodes for forecasted peak 120 QPS. Expected cache hit 25-35% which reduces compute by ~20-30%.
Cost sensitivity: target unit cost < $0.0009 per output token; procurement wants 12-month committed pricing with quarterly review. Preferred billing: reserved monthly + usage overage.
Security: Must run in VPC with customer-managed peering, KMS integration for key-wrapping, SOC2 report and SSO SAML for admin console. Data residency: US only for now.
Infra notes: customer uses GCP us-central; prefers Dedicated nodes co-located in that region. Networking team flagged NAT gateway egress limits for embedding-heavy workload.
Quotes/paraphrases: PM - 'We need consistent latency for SLAs or we won't sign enterprise deals.' SE - 'Cache and batching helped a lot in hosted trial, but we need control over autoscale behavior.'

Immediate next steps: customer to finalize list of enterprise accounts for pilot; Redwood to produce final SOW and 12-month capacity + pricing schedule; security deep-dive scheduled w/ legal week of 2026-03-15.
